clue.text: Glad Barney's moving on the whole

indicators.note: letters that are moving around are rearranged into a fresh order here

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, leaving the name as written

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that their friend Barney is moving on overall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' signals an anagram of GLAD and BARNEY, ten letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms meaning generally or in most respects.

clue.text: Curry dish served with extra American port

parts.note: a balti is a curry cooked and served in a metal bowl
more means additional or extra

explanation.surface: A restaurant serves a curry with an extra helping on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: A BALTI is a curry style popular in Britain, especially Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is a major seaport city in Maryland, USA.

clue.text: Similar first-rate variety died off

parts.note: A, as in A1, means first-rate

indicators.note: off means the letter for died is removed from the word for variety

parts.note: a kind is a variety or sort
D is the standard abbreviation for died in records

explanation.surface: A top-quality plant variety has died out, much like another one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' takes D (died) from KIND, leaving KIN after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means related or alike in character, a close synonym of similar.

clue.text: Shabby suit clothing journalist

parts.note: to do is to suit or be enough, as in 'that will do'
gear is informal for clothes
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is wearing a scruffy, worn-out suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like a container indicator, but it simply means GEAR in a plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages with folded corners look worn, so the word came to mean scruffy or worn-out.

clue.text: Share out about due turned up

parts.note: A is a recognised abbreviation for about, meaning approximately

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word for due is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a toll is a charge or payment due

explanation.surface: Someone divides money owed after it finally arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns TOLL into LLOT, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion portions among people.

clue.text: Hopeless case, the Italian, in Shakespearean role

parts.note: a goner is someone beyond help
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: An Italian actor is a lost cause in a Shakespeare part.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril is King Lear's eldest daughter in the tragedy, a famous character part.

clue.text: Second edition?

parts.note: read 'second' as earlier or behind, so an edition from the past rather than a reprint

explanation.surface: A publisher asks whether this is a second printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second edition' suggests a reprint, but the phrase means an old issue of a magazine or paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An earlier issue of a periodical is called this, back meaning past and number meaning issue.

clue.text: Music makers creating a stir?

definitions.meaning: pairs of these utensils are clacked together as a folk percussion instrument
these utensils stir tea or soup

explanation.surface: Musicians cause a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Clacked together they are a folk percussion instrument, and in a cup they are kitchen stirrers.

clue.text: Awful taking off without cover of darkness

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the mimicking word goes round the covering word

parts.note: taking off someone is mimicking them, aping
a pall is a dark covering, as a pall of smoke

explanation.surface: A dreadful plane taking off without lights in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: PALL goes inside APING, after AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalling describes something shockingly bad, a synonym of dreadful.

clue.text: Told to advance unaccompanied

indicators.note: told signals words spoken, so the money word is heard as a different spelling

parts.note: a loan is an advance of money

explanation.surface: A person was told to go forward on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: Lone means solitary, without companions.

clue.text: Clay and no amount of wood's taken over

indicators.note: taken over means the pair of words is turned right round, read backwards as one run

parts.note: nil means nothing, no amount at all
oak is a hardwood, possessive 's adding no letter

explanation.surface: Clay and timber are seized in a takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' reverses NIL OAK to give KAOLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaolin is the fine white china clay used in porcelain.

clue.text: Extremely delighted when in them?

parts.note: a state of ecstasy people are said to be 'in', as in the idiom 'in ...' meaning overjoyed

explanation.surface: People are overjoyed when inside something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being 'in raptures' is an idiom for being ecstatic, so these are states of great joy.

clue.text: Somehow Tessa needs to show decorum

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters get arranged in some unspecified new way

explanation.surface: Tessa is told she must behave properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' signals an anagram of TESSA and NEEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedateness is calm dignity of manner, akin to propriety and composure.

clue.text: High time report reaches final conclusion

annotationWithheld.why: High time report reaches final conclusion (6): UP (high) + SHOT (report) gives UPSHOT, but 'time' gives no letters and no reading finds a job for it; the clue may be misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: High time report reaches final conclusion

clue.text: Taken in by plot involving art

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the garden word wraps round the word for cunning

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
guile is cunning, artfulness

explanation.surface: Someone was fooled by a scheme involving fine art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a scheme but is a garden BED; 'involving' puts GUILE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beguiled is to be charmed or deceived, tricked.

clue.text: Subject to course stress

parts.note: under means subject to, as under orders
a line is a course or route taken

explanation.surface: Someone is subject to a course in emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline is to emphasise, as by drawing a rule beneath words.

clue.text: Gloomy composer seen around northern town

indicators.note: around means the gloomy word goes round the letter for northern

parts.note: sad means gloomy
J S Bach, the German Baroque composer

explanation.surface: A melancholy composer is spotted near a northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: SANDBACH is a market town in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandbach is a Cheshire market town, so it fits a bare definition of a place.

clue.text: Feel certain girl's ringing married poet

parts.note: to bet is to be sure, as in 'I bet'

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the girl's name goes round the letter for married

parts.note: Jean is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone is sure a girl is phoning her married poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' suggests a phone call but puts M inside JEAN. John Betjeman was a Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Betjeman was a British Poet Laureate, so he is an example of a versifier.

clue.text: One aunt is relaxing in foreign country

indicators.note: relaxing suggests loosening, so the letters are freed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One's aunt is on holiday relaxing abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relaxing' signals an anagram of I, AUNT and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African nation, so it serves as an overseas land.

clue.text: Confused by commercial break

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: Someone was bewildered by an advertising break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial break' looks like one phrase, but splits into AD and RIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrift means lost or bewildered, without direction.

clue.text: One infiltrating popular front to no avail

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so the numeral enters the other words

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spy infiltrates a popular movement but gets nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infiltrating' puts I inside VAN, after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means without success, uselessly.

clue.text: Frenchman's run around with European traitor

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name
to gad is to run around in search of pleasure

explanation.surface: A French man has been running around with a European betrayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade is one who deserts a cause, a turncoat.

clue.text: Rush after German displaying excessive appetite

indicators.note: after means the plant word follows the letter for German

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like plant

explanation.surface: Someone hurries after a German with a huge appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like a verb but is the waterside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is an overwhelming desire, especially for food or wealth.

clue.text: Urged campaign against new head

parts.note: a drive is a campaign, as a fundraising drive

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word new

explanation.surface: A campaign was pushed against the new boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' is a link meaning next to; 'new head' looks like a new boss but is just the first letter of new.
explanation.definitionFit: Driven means impelled or pushed forward.

clue.text: Told to try this place

indicators.note: told signals speech, so the court word is heard as a different spelling

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to attempt it at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' as in try a case: HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in or at this location.

clue.text: Land's a part of this leisure complex

indicators.note: a part of means the run of letters sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: The land forms part of this leisure complex.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, a piece of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Open main site housing key facilities

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the rearranged letters surround the key
open suggests prising the letters apart and rearranging them

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A main site opens, housing key facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' signals an anagram of MAIN SITE, which holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenities are useful features or services of a place.

clue.text: Searched wrong guy outside — it's bad luck

indicators.note: outside means the man's word goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: he refers to a man, a guy

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone searched for the wrong man, which was unfortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles SEARCHED into ARDCHEES, and 'outside' wraps HE round it. HARD CHEESE is British slang for tough luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for misfortune, used dismissively to mean too bad.
